title: Moriah + Zion: What Do the Names Mean?
subtitle: A textual-topographic concept explorer
summary: Explore how Moriah and Zion function across biblical texts and later association without reducing either name to a single timeless GPS coordinate.
disclaimer: Concept lenses explain textual and historical associations. Camera positions are teaching anchors on established or traditional geography; they do not assign coordinates to the unlocated Zion record or prove the Genesis 22 location archaeologically.

evidenceLegend.label: Known geography / archaeology
evidenceLegend.description: Established physical zones used as reference geography.

evidenceLegend.label: Textual-historical inference
evidenceLegend.description: A relationship inferred by comparing how names are used across texts and periods.

evidenceLegend.label: Canonical / later association
evidenceLegend.description: A traditional or canonical association kept separate from direct archaeological identification.

evidenceLegend.label: Not exactly locatable
evidenceLegend.description: The text or evidence does not support a precise modern point.

entryCamera.note: Teaching camera between the southeastern ridge and Temple Mount precinct; it is not a coordinate for either biblical toponym.

comparison.label: Moriah and Zion lenses
comparison.intro: Select a lens to see what the relevant text actually establishes and what later association or interpretation adds.

options.label: Zion in 2 Samuel 5
options.summary: In David's capture narrative, Zion is associated with the stronghold and the City of David context.
options.rationale: 2 Samuel 5 directly links the stronghold of Zion with the City of David. The southeastern ridge provides the archaeological/topographic reference zone used by the existing atlas.
options.objections: The Zion atlas record intentionally remains unlocated because later biblical uses expand beyond this early association. The camera must not be read as a permanent Zion coordinate.

camera.note: Camera points to the southeastern-ridge context used to explain the early textual association; it does not assign coordinates to Zion itself.

options.label: Zion in later usage
options.summary: Later biblical texts can use Zion more broadly for Jerusalem, its sacred center, or the community associated with it.
options.rationale: The change in usage is itself the teaching point: a toponym can broaden semantically over time rather than remain one tiny mapped feature.
options.objections: This prototype does not draw a period-by-period Zion polygon because the textual term is not equivalent to a recoverable cadastral boundary.

camera.note: Broader Jerusalem framing illustrates semantic expansion; it is not a mapped boundary of later Zion.

options.label: Moriah in Genesis 22
options.summary: Genesis 22 sends Abraham to the land of Moriah but does not provide a modern survey coordinate for the mountain.
options.rationale: The responsible visualization begins with the textual statement and leaves exact geography unresolved before later canonical association is considered.
options.objections: A Temple Mount camera would overstate what Genesis 22 alone establishes; this lens therefore uses Jerusalem only as a neutral display frame rather than claiming the event occurred at that point.

camera.note: Neutral Jerusalem display frame for comparing the later association; this is expressly not a Genesis 22 event coordinate.

options.label: Moriah in 2 Chronicles 3:1
options.summary: 2 Chronicles 3:1 names Mount Moriah as the site where Solomon began building the temple, creating the canonical basis for the Jerusalem/Temple Mount association.
options.rationale: This later canonical text is why Jewish and Christian interpretation connects Genesis Moriah with Jerusalem's temple location.
options.objections: Canonical association is not the same category as direct archaeological confirmation of Abraham's location or an exact First Temple footprint.

camera.note: Camera uses the existing traditional Moriah/Temple Mount association and must remain visually labeled as traditional rather than identified-site.

options.label: Temple Mount as physical precinct
options.summary: The Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif is an identifiable physical precinct even when exact period-specific temple footprints remain uncertain.
options.rationale: Separating physical geography from reconstructed architecture lets the atlas show what is securely locatable without overclaiming the inaccessible First Temple footprint.
options.objections: The present precinct cannot simply be treated as an unchanged surface for every biblical period, and this lens does not reconstruct the sanctuary building.

camera.note: Camera centers the established physical precinct while withholding any claimed First Temple building footprint.

hotspots.label: Zion record: deliberately unlocated
hotspots.summary: The underlying v1 Zion record has no coordinates so changing biblical usage is not converted into false precision.

whyShown.evidence: The Zion atlas record intentionally omits coordinates.
whyShown.inference: This interactive hotspot must occupy a screen/map location to be clickable, so its placement is a display device tied to the active explanatory lens, not Zion's stored coordinate.
whyShown.alternatives: Later uses of Zion can broaden toward Jerusalem and the temple; future visual layers should teach that shift rather than move a single authoritative pin.

hotspots.label: Southeastern ridge reference
hotspots.summary: Established archaeological/topographic reference for explaining the early City of David/Zion association.

whyShown.evidence: The southeastern ridge is an established archaeological zone containing Jerusalem's earliest urban core.
whyShown.inference: It is used as a reference zone for the early Zion/City of David textual association without claiming every biblical phrase maps to the same boundaries.

hotspots.label: Genesis 22 location limit
hotspots.summary: Genesis names the land of Moriah but does not itself identify a modern coordinate.

whyShown.evidence: The textual place-name is real, but the exact geography is not supplied as a modern coordinate by Genesis 22.
whyShown.inference: The hotspot sits at the later Jerusalem association only because this scene compares that association; it is not evidence that Abraham stood here.

hotspots.label: Moriah / Temple Mount association
hotspots.summary: The canonical association rests especially on 2 Chronicles 3:1 and is represented with a traditional-site role.

whyShown.evidence: 2 Chronicles explicitly connects Mount Moriah with Solomon's temple location.
whyShown.inference: The atlas represents that association at the Temple Mount precinct as traditional/canonical geography, not as independent archaeological proof of Genesis 22.

hotspots.label: Physical precinct vs. temple footprint
hotspots.summary: An established precinct can be mapped even when an exact ancient sanctuary footprint is not available.

whyShown.evidence: The Temple Mount/Haram al-Sharif precinct is a physically identifiable location.
whyShown.inference: The scene uses it as geographic context while declining to draw an exact First Temple building footprint.
whyShown.alternatives: Future period models can show multiple scholarly reconstructions, each labeled as interpretive rather than measured archaeology.
